profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer

positions.title: Teaching Assistant - ME116M: Introduction to the Design of Smart Products
positions.description: As one of two teaching assistants for the course, I assisted professors Ed Carryer and Sean Follmer as well as lecturer Alex Olwal in the first year of a new mechatronics course. Being the first year the course was offered, my duties included the development of the new curriculum in addition to the normal pedagogical duties of a TA. I assisted students with PCB design, software engineering, and interface design; more broadly, the teaching team focused on building students' familiarity with modern rapid prototyping tools & techniques and the fundamentals of interaction design.

positions.title: Teaching Assisant - ME218: Smart Product Design
positions.description: ME218 is a three quarter masters level embedded systems and mechatronics design sequence (ME218) at Stanford University, the first two quarters of which I was the teaching assistant for. As the TA, I was responsible for assisting teams of engineering graduate students with multiple quarter long mechatronics projects. In addition, I improved and built class infrastructure and tools and instructed students on embedded programming as well as digital and analog systems.

positions.title: Hardware & Firmware Engineer
positions.description:
Made up half of the hardware team at SAM Labs, a startup making Bluetooth enabled modules with various sensors and electronic elements to be used for electronics education and prototyping. 
Re-wrote the firmware base in order to implement support for over the air updates; updated a manufacturer issued iOS app to serve as the host for the OTA process. 
Designed two new products from the ground up, including schematic layout, pcb design, prototype assembly, and firmware development. 
Designed and built a development board for internal use. 
Wrote test and programming Python scripts for a mass-programmer array that reduced programming and functional testing times by a factor of 10

positions.title: Research Assistant - ME Summer Undergraduate Research Institute (SURI)
positions.description:
Conducted a research project under the umbrella of the Center for Design Research (CDR) and the Center for Integrated Facility Engineering (CIFE).
Examined datasets from Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) projects to determine the effectiveness of various approaches to project development (Integrated Project Delivery, Integrated Concurrent Engineering, pull-planning, co-location).
Wrote Python scripts to examine output logs from version control and 4D Building Information Modeling software in order to determine degrees of communication, collaboration, and information flow between the numerous stakeholders in AEC projects.
Compared and contrasted quantitative data with interviews, reports, and other qualitative information.
